# Reward provenance determines where credit belongs

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/post-training/reward-and-credit.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-26 · 50 topic entries / 20 representative comparisons

Process labels, final outcomes, self-confidence, and hindsight attribution are distinct evidence. Stepwise PRMs, MRTPO, TACO, and MART-GRPO obtain labels, localize reward, damp positive credit, and filter failed suffixes respectively. INTUITOR uses an intrinsic distributional signal, not external verification. CONCUR instead prioritizes reward dimensions by projecting gated auxiliary advantages onto a primary-reward order cone; it does not assign token credit over time.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Automatic process labels are not unconditional step truth

Human supervision asks whether a particular step is valid. Math-Shepherd estimates whether sampling from it eventually yields a correct answer, reflecting the continuation policy's ability to recover and finish. INTUITOR reads only model distributions, without final-answer correctness. Distinguish label meaning before comparing cost.

Sources: [Let's Verify Step by Step](../../../../post-training/2305.20050-process-supervision/README-en.md) · [Math-Shepherd](../../../../post-training/2312.08935-math-shepherd/README-en.md) · [INTUITOR](../../../../post-training/2505.19590-intuitor/README-en.md)

### Credit filters act on different quantities and preserve different invariants

TACO attenuates positive advantages only. MART-GRPO masks failed-episode credit after a hindsight error boundary without changing the denominator. MRTPO redistributes signed credit across verifier information blocks with total and magnitude constraints. Deleting suspicious tokens and re-averaging cannot reproduce them all.

Sources: [TACO](../../../../post-training/2607.07976-taco/README-en.md) · [When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2610.32431-mart-grpo/README-en.md) · [Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL](../../../../post-training/2610.21439-mrtpo/README-en.md)

### Reward priorities and token credit use different axes

TACO lowers positive credit within one response by local risk and preserves negative credit. CONCUR compares primary and auxiliary rewards across responses to the same prompt, adjusting standardized auxiliary order and ceiling differences. It does not identify a faulty token. A scalar loses both the nearest projection and sign separation. A ceiling tie removes that auxiliary's ordering for the group, not gradient training entirely.

Sources: [CONCUR: Concordant Auxiliary Rewards for Multi-Task, Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2610.36437-concur/README-en.md) · [TACO](../../../../post-training/2607.07976-taco/README-en.md)

### Outcome density is a group-level coordinate, not token risk or primary-reward priority

TACO reduces positive token credit by local tail risk while preserving negative credit. CONCUR projects within-group auxiliary advantages to respect primary-reward order. DARS acts elsewhere: crowding among outcome representations under the same prompt. It scales nonnegative terminal rewards by Gaussian density including self before computing group advantages. Equal raw rewards can become unequal after density scaling; zero variance concerns the scaled rewards. Duplicate points retain multiplicity at narrow bandwidth instead of universally approaching density one. Embeddings, bandwidth and std conventions define this coordinate; synthetic KDE checks are not policy coverage or image-quality evidence.

Sources: [Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling](../../../../post-training/2611.04792-dars/README-en.md) · [TACO](../../../../post-training/2607.07976-taco/README-en.md) · [CONCUR: Concordant Auxiliary Rewards for Multi-Task, Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2610.36437-concur/README-en.md)

### Fuse the video reward, or allocate it across generation tokens?

EmoReward calibrates one scalar per video across score providers, using current validity and proxy correlations from a completed run. TVRL redistributes an existing group advantage along the generation-token axis using input gradients from a frozen VLM. A scalar does not identify which tokens caused an effect; a gradient attribution does not estimate whether facial or motion providers remain reliable across runs. Control the provider set and credit allocator separately in comparisons.

Sources: [EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL](../../../../post-training/2611.06518-emoreward/README-en.md) · [Token-Level Video Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2610.01973-tvrl/README-en.md)

### Useful rewards and token attribution are separate; conserved credit does not validate a reward

MaxIM defines how task information and factual consistency become rewards. MCPO takes a supplied sequence advantage and changes relative token weights. MCPO's preserved response mean cannot repair a mistaken critic, and MaxIM's critic does not automatically provide correct token attribution. Check privileged leakage on the reward side, old versus current policy on the credit side, and whether generation length changes the real budget.

Sources: [MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2611.12825-maxim/README-en.md) · [Margin-Guided Token Credit for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards](../../../../post-training/2611.14015-mcpo/README-en.md)

### Completion self-judgment credit differs from token-level teacher–student residuals

RLMF separates faithfulness and other constraints, boosting only positive faithfulness deviations according to self-judgment accuracy; the group mean may become nonzero. Residual Advantage uses full-vocabulary teacher–student differences, a student-expectation baseline and response-position centering before adding verifier credit. Co-RA updates its teacher on a fixed scored batch and uses it next round. Adding Z as reward, conflating token residuals with completion advantages or recentering RLMF changes these methods. Their evidence and update units remain separate; an RA checkpoint smoke does not train RLMF.

Sources: [Reinforcement Learning with Metacognitive Feedback Elicits Faithful Uncertainty Expression in LLMs](../../../../post-training/2606.32032-rlmf/README-en.md) · [Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards](../../../../post-training/2610.11519-residual-advantage/README-en.md)

### Specify probe provenance before deciding which reward object to transform

TAG trains one policy per reward from a common baseline and selects an anchor with reverse KL on probe-generated samples. Bait privately marks special responses, compares environment reward preferences and flips the whole group. Both need actual probe provenance, not evaluator gold manufacturing perfect signals. Local Bait generates no text or attack: it checks the >=0 boundary and policy-only output. TAG's zero-anchor gating does not replace this sign rule.

Sources: [Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function](../../../../post-training/2611.16369-bait-reward-defense/README-en.md) · [Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense](../../../../post-training/2610.21404-tag-reward-gating/README-en.md)

### Why is rising GPR not sufficient evidence of reward escape?

GPR divides by remaining harm, whereas PHR divides by all harmful-prompt responses. Known harm can fall faster, increasing the blind-spot share while its amount declines. Escape requires significantly rising PHR and external audit. Bait transforms rewards from a private probe/policy reward gap. This protocol audits gated misses and temporal changes; it does not automatically flip rewards or treat one reference judge as absolute truth. Local boundary: Confidence gate, held-out calibration threshold, distinct PHR/GPR denominators, prompt-level bootstrap and judge-version revalidation; no commercial judge implementation.

Sources: [Jev-as-a-Reward: Validating Probabilistic Safety Judges for Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2611.20955-jev-safety-reward/README-en.md) · [Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function](../../../../post-training/2611.16369-bait-reward-defense/README-en.md)

### Why can sufficiency-only rewards encourage padding?

Citing every feature may be sufficient while including irrelevant material. The exact reward uses the MSR union for precision and the best individual MSR for recall, so padding lowers precision. No. It audits proxy selection error and reward gaps where truth is enumerable; Bait applies a probe-based defense. Such exact oracles are domain-limited and do not solve general agent truth. Local boundary: Exact MSR antichains on small finite state spaces, causal precision/recall/F1 and proxy selection-error/signed/absolute gaps; no simulated LLM damage claims.

Sources: [Optimistic Verifiers Get Hacked: Reward Hacking Under an Exact Process Oracle](../../../../post-training/2611.21538-optimistic-verifier-audit/README-en.md) · [Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function](../../../../post-training/2611.16369-bait-reward-defense/README-en.md)

### May the V4 expert panel be added directly to composite reward?

No. Experts determine signal admission and score blinded canaries. Reward aggregates only function/design/rubric/preference channels, while build/render/anticheat and other V0 gates multiply it. Bait detects private-probe reward preferences and flips rewards. This method admits and revalidates candidate judging signals. Probe coverage and expert golden/trap coverage are different assumptions, neither a universal guarantee. Local boundary: Four admission tests for expert agreement, causal sensitivity, hack resistance and stability; multiplicative V0 hard gates and admitted-score composite reward, not a browser or design judge.

Sources: [Learning Design Taste through Verifiable Synthetic Environments and Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2611.20612-design-taste-admission/README-en.md) · [Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function](../../../../post-training/2611.16369-bait-reward-defense/README-en.md)

### Why is full-trajectory scoring cheaper offline than online?

Offline diagnosis and best-of-N already have completed candidates. Step-wise search must generate continuations before judging the current step; cost cannot be estimated as ordinary prefix-only PRM scoring. Bait defensively transforms an external probe/policy reward gap, not reasoning-step correctness. GPRM learns a four-axis process model with predicted history and future trajectories. Both require scorer isolation, but neither Bait algebra nor a label parser substitutes for a PRM. Local boundary: Method and cost review only; no string parser or fixed rule replaces the four-dimensional global PRM.

Sources: [GPRM: Global Perspective Process Reward Model](../../../../post-training/2611.20755-gprm/README-en.md) · [Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function](../../../../post-training/2611.16369-bait-reward-defense/README-en.md)

### Are ECA and OpCredit the same process reward?

OpCredit combines reused branch-outcome credit with answer-neighborhood frontier credit for KG operations. ECA uses a frozen model's answer likelihood from retrieved text as its potential. Both align training credit to operation spans, but their states and potentials are not interchangeable, and neither permits training gold in the actor. No. It accepts external training-potential values, rewards and span masks, not answer text, and implements no evaluated agent. Reference answers belong only to an isolated training scorer; inference actors see legitimate questions, history and observations.

Sources: [Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models](../../../../post-training/2611.23824-eca-credit/README-en.md) · [OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering](../../../../post-training/2610.21345-opcredit/README-en.md)

### Do DCC and DynamicRubric act at the same point?

DynamicRubric changes evaluation criteria and weights while co-evolving with the policy. DCC treats rubric, judge and weights as given, fitting shared clipping endpoints from the current group's numeric scores. They address different levels—evaluator adaptation versus score-scale effects—and an aggregator is not a dynamic judge. Two-medians can isolate an extreme in its own cluster, making that value the upper endpoint. DCC offers a conditional contribution bound, not universal outlier removal or capability improvement.

Sources: [How Reward Gain Imbalance Shapes Ranking: Rethinking Rubric-Based Reward Aggregation](../../../../post-training/2611.24005-dcc-aggregation/README-en.md) · [Co-Evolving LLM Evaluators and Policies via DynamicRubric](../../../../reproductions/2607.20083-dynamic-rubric/README-en.md)

### Local credit can come from matched trajectories or a global tree posterior

Re-reading OpCredit confirms deduplicated context-matched BOC supports and operation-local FTC frontiers, without gold in actor inputs. BRIAR treats a sampled prefix tree as a Gaussian state-space model; upward information and downward smoothing transmit sibling evidence. Dense covariance is an independent numerical reference. Equation5's2.2 factor and length term do not impose a hard martingale variance bound, and excluding prefix-token loss does not freeze shared-parameter prefix behavior. CPU equivalence only supports the numerical component; the full16/32-A100 matrix is too expensive.

Sources: [BRIAR: Martingale Belief Smoothing on Bifurcation-Guided Reasoning Trees](../../../../post-training/2611.34746-briar/README-en.md) · [OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering](../../../../post-training/2610.21345-opcredit/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Is a low Math-Shepherd continuation success rate equivalent to a human PRM finding a logically wrong step? {#cross-step-truth-versus-continuation}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Subsequent sampling and budget affect the rate; correct steps can lead to difficult continuations. A human label evaluates the step itself. Both can help, but automatic labels are not logical ground truth. Keep training answers out of evaluated model inputs.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: A correct equation followed by arithmetic the model cannot finish can yield zero successful continuations without invalidating the equation.

    Sources: [Let's Verify Step by Step](../../../../post-training/2305.20050-process-supervision/README-en.md) · [Math-Shepherd](../../../../post-training/2312.08935-math-shepherd/README-en.md)

### Why not implement TACO and MART-GRPO by deleting tokens and averaging again? {#cross-filter-denominator}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** TACO preserves negative credit and damps risky positive credit. MART-GRPO zeros a failed suffix but keeps the original valid-action-token denominator. Re-averaging amplifies remaining terms and changes the objective. MRTPO separately preserves total credit through redistribution.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: After masking the last four of ten tokens, dividing by six instead of ten makes remaining negative terms stronger than MART defines.

    Sources: [TACO](../../../../post-training/2607.07976-taco/README-en.md) · [When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2610.32431-mart-grpo/README-en.md) · [Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL](../../../../post-training/2610.21439-mrtpo/README-en.md)

### Is a sharper INTUITOR distribution the same reward improvement as more correct Math-Shepherd continuations? {#cross-confidence-is-not-verification}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. INTUITOR uses full-vocabulary KL(U∥policy); Math-Shepherd measures final correctness. Models can be confidently wrong, and reversing KL changes the quantity. The local candidate diagnostic lacks the original direction and per-token full-vocabulary calculation, so do not rank capabilities with it.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: A model can always select one wrong number sharply while its verified continuation success remains zero.

    Sources: [INTUITOR](../../../../post-training/2505.19590-intuitor/README-en.md) · [Math-Shepherd](../../../../post-training/2312.08935-math-shepherd/README-en.md)

### Why can't CONCUR simply reuse TACO risk weights or reduce the length reward coefficient? {#cross-concur-reward-axis-not-token-filter}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** TACO dampens positive token credit to avoid reinforcing local errors. CONCUR ensures a higher primary-reward response does not receive a lower gated auxiliary score and can merge ceiling scores. Scaling leaves existing inversions intact and does not give a nearest order-preserving projection.

    **Illustrative example:** Illustration: Correctness scores 0.6 and 0.9 may have standardized length scores 1 and −1. Multiplying both length scores by 0.1 keeps the inversion, and token risk cannot order the two responses by correctness.

    Sources: [CONCUR: Concordant Auxiliary Rewards for Multi-Task, Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2610.36437-concur/README-en.md) · [TACO](../../../../post-training/2607.07976-taco/README-en.md)

### With every raw reward equal to one, must DARS yield the same zero advantages as unmodified group normalization? {#cross-outcome-density-not-token-or-priority}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Unequal densities can turn equal raw rewards into unequal scaled values, yielding nonzero relative signals after normalization. The zero-variance check must use scaled rewards. TACO calibrates positive credit by token risk, while CONCUR constrains auxiliary ranking by primary reward; equal raw rewards do not make either equivalent to DARS. They consume different evidence and act on different coordinates.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: For y=(0,0,100), a very narrow bandwidth and r=(1,1,1), self-inclusive densities are about (2,2,1), producing nonconstant scaled rewards (0.5,0.5,1). Three coincident outcomes instead share a density and retain constant scaled rewards.

    Sources: [Density-Aware Reward Scaling: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Reward-Proportional Sampling](../../../../post-training/2611.04792-dars/README-en.md) · [TACO](../../../../post-training/2607.07976-taco/README-en.md) · [CONCUR: Concordant Auxiliary Rewards for Multi-Task, Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2610.36437-concur/README-en.md)

### If two videos have the same final emotion scalar, must EmoReward and TVRL assign the same credit to their generation tokens? {#cross-emoreward-vs-tvrl-credit-axis}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. EmoReward outputs a video-level scalar, not token credit. TVRL distributes an existing group advantage using gradients from a frozen VLM. Two videos with the same scalar can have different token sensitivities. Attribution cannot create nonzero credit when the underlying group advantage is zero.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Suppose both videos have positive advantages in one group. Foreground movement matters more in one video, while a later transition matters more in the other. TVRL sensitivities can differ; EmoReward does not emit that allocation.

    Sources: [EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL](../../../../post-training/2611.06518-emoreward/README-en.md) · [Token-Level Video Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2610.01973-tvrl/README-en.md)

### Would applying MCPO to MaxIM rewards guarantee more factual memory? {#cross-reward-versus-token-redistribution}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. They can affect different stages, but approximate information rewards, token-credit heuristics and inference-input isolation require separate validation. Preserving mean sequence advantage is only an arithmetic contract; it proves neither critic correctness nor factual summaries or task improvement.

    **Illustrative example:** If a critic wrongly rewards a fabricated budget, MCPO can still distribute that positive advantage by token margin. The mean is exactly conserved while the wrong direction is reinforced.

    Sources: [MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2611.12825-maxim/README-en.md) · [Margin-Guided Token Credit for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards](../../../../post-training/2611.14015-mcpo/README-en.md)

### Can RLMF's metacognitive Z and Residual Advantage's teacher–student residual be directly added as the same token reward? {#cross-cross-rlmf-versus-dr-grpo}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Z measures completion FC self-judgment error and scales positive group-relative faithfulness only. RA uses tokenwise full-vocabulary q−p, subtracts a student-expectation baseline, response-centers, then adds verifier credit. A combination needs a new explicit definition and validation.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: RLMF with f=[0,1,2], o=[1,0,−1], Z1 yields[0,0,1], mean1/3. A response's centered RA residuals[0.2,−0.2] have mean0. Forcing both to zero mean changes RLMF.

    Sources: [Reinforcement Learning with Metacognitive Feedback Elicits Faithful Uncertainty Expression in LLMs](../../../../post-training/2606.32032-rlmf/README-en.md) · [Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards](../../../../post-training/2610.11519-residual-advantage/README-en.md)

### Can a trusted TAG anchor directly serve as Bait's private probe mask? {#cross-cross-nov15-bait-tag-probe}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. TAG selects a reward dimension through trained probe policies; Bait membership identifies response provenance within a group. Inputs, sampling and trust assumptions differ and need separate verification. Neither numeric core establishes the other's real safety.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: in a group of three responses, a TAG correctness-anchor score does not identify which response came from a defender probe.

    Sources: [Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function](../../../../post-training/2611.16369-bait-reward-defense/README-en.md) · [Multi-Reward Hacking: From Aggregation-Induced Drift to Trust-Anchored Defense](../../../../post-training/2610.21404-tag-reward-gating/README-en.md)

### How does it relate to Bait reward-sign flipping? {#cross-nov18-jev-safety-reward}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Bait transforms rewards from a private probe/policy reward gap. This protocol audits gated misses and temporal changes; it does not automatically flip rewards or treat one reference judge as absolute truth.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a PHR interval containing zero calls for S3, not negation of every training reward.

    Sources: [Jev-as-a-Reward: Validating Probabilistic Safety Judges for Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2611.20955-jev-safety-reward/README-en.md) · [Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function](../../../../post-training/2611.16369-bait-reward-defense/README-en.md)

### Does it repair rewards like Bait? {#cross-nov18-optimistic-verifier-audit}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. It audits proxy selection error and reward gaps where truth is enumerable; Bait applies a probe-based defense. Such exact oracles are domain-limited and do not solve general agent truth.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a proxy tie between unequal true rewards contributes .5 selection error, which diagnoses selection distortion rather than observed training damage.

    Sources: [Optimistic Verifiers Get Hacked: Reward Hacking Under an Exact Process Oracle](../../../../post-training/2611.21538-optimistic-verifier-audit/README-en.md) · [Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function](../../../../post-training/2611.16369-bait-reward-defense/README-en.md)

### Why is this distinct from Bait despite both addressing reward hacking? {#cross-nov18-design-taste-admission}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Bait detects private-probe reward preferences and flips rewards. This method admits and revalidates candidate judging signals. Probe coverage and expert golden/trap coverage are different assumptions, neither a universal guarantee.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: expert agreement .99 but trap-failure .21 rejects admission rather than negating the metric.

    Sources: [Learning Design Taste through Verifiable Synthetic Environments and Agentic Reinforcement Learning](../../../../post-training/2611.20612-design-taste-admission/README-en.md) · [Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function](../../../../post-training/2611.16369-bait-reward-defense/README-en.md)

### Can GPRM be obtained by adding a label parser to the existing Bait reward-defense component? {#cross-nov18-gprm}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Bait defensively transforms an external probe/policy reward gap, not reasoning-step correctness. GPRM learns a four-axis process model with predicted history and future trajectories. Both require scorer isolation, but neither Bait algebra nor a label parser substitutes for a PRM.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Bait reward flipping does not assess consistency of a reasoning step with later derivation; parsing [CORRECT] is not judging it correctly.

    Sources: [GPRM: Global Perspective Process Reward Model](../../../../post-training/2611.20755-gprm/README-en.md) · [Bait: Mitigating Harmful Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Probing Reward Function](../../../../post-training/2611.16369-bait-reward-defense/README-en.md)

### Are ECA and OpCredit the same process reward? {#cross-nov19-eca-credit}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. OpCredit's FTC depends on KG answer neighborhoods and operation-local frontiers, whereas ECA depends on a frozen policy's reference-answer likelihood from deduplicated text. Shared operation-local assignment does not make the potentials interchangeable.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a retrieved passage can improve answer-token likelihood without defining an active entity frontier in a one-hop KG neighborhood.

    Sources: [Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models](../../../../post-training/2611.23824-eca-credit/README-en.md) · [OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering](../../../../post-training/2610.21345-opcredit/README-en.md)

### Do DCC and DynamicRubric act at the same point? {#cross-nov19-dcc-aggregation}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. DynamicRubric generates or updates criteria and weights; DCC holds those semantics fixed and transforms existing score ranges. Weights enter only the final average, not center estimation.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: changing a criterion weight from1 to100 changes rewards but not the fitted endpoints of the same score matrix.

    Sources: [How Reward Gain Imbalance Shapes Ranking: Rethinking Rubric-Based Reward Aggregation](../../../../post-training/2611.24005-dcc-aggregation/README-en.md) · [Co-Evolving LLM Evaluators and Policies via DynamicRubric](../../../../reproductions/2607.20083-dynamic-rubric/README-en.md)

### Can trajectories at the same entity be merged into a shared BRIAR prefix? {#cross-nov26-briar-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Full visible histories must match. OpCredit likewise needs context matching: identical entities do not imply identical visited sets, budgets or phases. Ignoring history conflates conditional probabilities and credit.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: one trajectory has visitedA with one step left; another has not and has three steps left. Their continuation distributions differ despite the same current entity.

    Sources: [BRIAR: Martingale Belief Smoothing on Bifurcation-Guided Reasoning Trees](../../../../post-training/2611.34746-briar/README-en.md) · [OpCredit: Operation-Aware Policy Learning for Agentic Knowledge Graph Question Answering](../../../../post-training/2610.21345-opcredit/README-en.md)
